reason: E1 directly supports that an oxide film formed in an oxidizing environment reduces wear compared to an inert atmosphere, but it is for a different alloy system (TiNbZrAg). E2 supports the role of frictional heating in oxidation but does not provide evidence for CoCrFeMnNi specifically. The key premise that CoCrFeMnNi forms a self-healing oxide tribofilm is not directly supported by the cited evidence.
premises: Frictional heating during wear can cause oxidation of alloy surfaces.
An oxide tribofilm formed in-situ during wear can significantly reduce wear rates.
The wear reduction by an oxide film is environment-dependent, being absent in inert atmospheres.
CoCrFeMnNi HEA can form a protective oxide under tribological conditions.
